brief: Today's posts centered on agents and the tools builders use to work with them, including evals, permission prompts on macOS, and design with Claude. Beyond that, Guillermo Rauch and Garry Tan described software as personalized and self-owned, and Garry Tan previewed a Rust GBrain backend.

themes.label: Agents as users and collaborators
themes.summary: Builders described agents as users of software and as collaborators, with Rauch saying evals now replace user interviews.

themes.label: Owning your AI stack
themes.summary: Builders argued for open SDKs, owned models and data, and personalized open source software.

themes.label: Coding and token spend trends
themes.summary: Builders said coding models now work for many tasks and token use is still rising, with infrastructure shifting from vibe coding to harnesses, sandboxes and agentic CI.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary: Argued that token spend per employee has no ceiling and that coding models are now working, which is leading to tool and computer use.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Posted a four-step roadmap for owning intelligence, and said a new era of personalized, open source software is here. Also said Vercel now runs evals in place of user interviews.

builders.name: Latent Space
builders.summary: Published a podcast episode with Mihail Eric of Monaco on how Stanford teaches AI-native engineering.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Shared top takeaways from @nateparrott on getting Claude to design without AI slop, and questioned a post about Megaspeed.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Said software factories are a temporary problem and that the key question is building workspaces where agents collaborate with people. Also shared a game character built with agents.

builders.name: Peter Steinberger
builders.summary: Complained that Apple's new macOS alerts add more permission prompts that interrupt agents working on macOS.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Floated proof of work as a feed ranking method, where agents report tokens used on content.

builders.name: Josh Woodward
builders.summary: Showed interactive sites made from sources with Gemini Notebook, and posted a short welcome message.

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.summary: Outlined 2026 infra phases from vibe coding to agentic CI and asked what comes next.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Said their interpretability work reached the point of applying it to leading frontier models, and announced a $24M seed round for BharatSemi.

builders.name: Garry Tan
builders.summary: Previewed a Rust GBrain backend to replace Postgres for vector search, and announced Degla drone autonomy for search and rescue.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Posted brief reactions, with the most-liked post a one-line jab at a cult.

builders.name: Google Labs
builders.summary: Welcomed the Howie team to Google Labs to build AI tools for small businesses.

builders.name: Nan Yu
builders.summary: Posted brief personal reactions with no substantive content.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Posted brief personal and off-topic remarks with no substantive content.
